report_notes.disposition: The report correctly distinguishes positive quadratic form/injectivity from a positive uniform lower operator bound. Both source versions explicitly prove the former. Compact injective K on infinite-dimensional L2 need not and here does not have K>=cI. No source correction required.
The adjacent multiplier 2lambda/(lambda^2+xi^2) is correct under the stated unitary Fourier convention; this garbled word is cosmetic, not a normalization defect. Raw report remains unchanged.

mathematical_checks: The report uses the actual upstream N(f)=||f||2^(1-alpha/4)||grad f||2^(alpha/4). On real Fourier band j, ||grad f_j||2<=2^j||f_j||2, so N(f_j)<=2^(j alpha/4)||f_j||2. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz sums these bounds because s>alpha/4, with sum 2^(2js)||f_j||2^2<=2^(2s)||f||Hs^2, including the factor-one low band. The H1 product extension is Cauchy by telescoping differences and the absolute four-linear estimate; bilinear Hilbert product norms contribute sqrt(R_sp), two band sums give C_s^2, and four absolute band sums give C_s^4 R_sp. Absolute L2 band convergence and the supplied null-set transfer justify physical versus Hilbert pairings. This verifies the added dyadic argument without assuming an Lp multiplier theorem.

The exact row is k(z,w)=(eta_R z1+c1 eta_R)(eta_R Lambda^-1 w2). The report correctly uses Lambda^-1:H^-1/2→H^1/2, then the supplied cutoff theorem at sigma=s, gamma=1/2-s>0 on both localized factors. Continuous fractional multiplication sends their compact closures into a compact H_sp row set. The row norm bound descends through covariance-null classes. Smooth compact potentials give compact H^1/2→H^-1/2 multiplication at gain one; the c1 column is finite rank and instantaneous c2 column zero, while free conjugation later retains both physical constant columns. Strong orthogonal projections are uniformly small on the compact row set by the explicit finite-net argument, giving finite-rank-map convergence and compactness of T_sp itself, not merely compact values.

This unchanged proof is explicitly read and its public account identifies all logical stages. Separated smooth tests factor by absolute Fubini after both null quotients. A common compact spatial A and uniform error epsilon give epsilon^2 |A| Gamma(A-A) times the finite double time-kernel integral; thus smooth time partitions times spatial slices are dense, as are countable smooth approximants on exhausting compact sets. Gram-Schmidt omitting null vectors preserves smooth supported representatives. The completed isometry has closed image H_I in H_W; its finite projection is orthogonal on H_W. This proves a supported Hilbert subspace, not time-indicator multiplication or independence. The public account is concise about this unchanged quantitative estimate, but does not replace the tensor conclusion with an external lemma or omit a critical logical ingredient.

With unitary Fourier, the e^(-lambda |v|) convolution quadratic form has multiplier 2lambda/(lambda^2+xi^2): the sqrt(2pi) convolution factor cancels that in the unitary transform of the kernel. Positive Gamma mixing lambda^(a-1)/Gamma_E(a) and Schur integrability give form positivity/injectivity. Hilbert-Schmidt deterministic truncations approximate K in norm with error<=2epsilon^(1-a)/(1-a); they are not claimed Gaussian covariances. Orthogonality to Ran K^(1/2) means membership in its zero kernel, so the completed isometry iota is onto. For 2<r<2/a, K_a lies in L^(r/2); the three Holder exponents r,(1/u-1/r)^-1,(1/v-1/r)^-1 have reciprocal sum one for u=r/2,v=rprime, giving Young, covariance-CS and duality. Interpolating a convergent L2 subsequence and bounded Lr2 differences gives compactness in Lr. A cell integral equals 2N^(a-2)/((1-a)(2-a)); normalization N and N cells yield trace sum 2N^a/((1-a)(2-a)), excluding trace class and Hilbert-Schmidt C_t. The report nuance is correct: strict positivity means positive quadratic form on nonzero vectors, not K>=cI.

For finite spatial fields, positivity of the scalar time kernel bounds the Hilbert time norm by the corresponding kernel form of pointwise vector norms, then scalar Young and finite-dimensional Lr duality yield a constant independent of dimension. The stated pointwise norming direction and coefficient approximation justify duality before completion. Tensor density gives strongly measurable UΦ; T_sp applies spatial covariance once. Smooth supported-control approximation identifies the physical masked multiplier; arbitrary H controls are completed K(F)-valued fields, not asserted pointwise potentials. Finite spatial Q_n leave finitely many compact scalar temporal coordinate maps; a finite diagonal subsequence proves T_n compact. Norm approximation using ||T_sp(I-Q_n)|| then gives T compact, and a weak-null residual sequence proves ||T(I-P_J)||→0. All compactness fixes R, with no infinite-identity tensor inference or uniform-radius tail.

The actual pullback has covariance factor delta^(a-2)delta^2 delta^-a=1, so Q_J orthogonality gives Var Y<=||f||HW^2. Supplied Gaussian transfer and the true F extension apply on a common coupled original W; theta<beta<beta2 below the stated threshold gives stopped paths in the separable little-Ctheta closure. For each observed smooth-state/true-column row, the slow pullback lies in H_I by compact-support covariance dominated convergence including endpoints. Because Ran P_J⊂H_I, subtracting P_J preserves H_I. Projecting the transfer to H_I leaves those rows unchanged, and countable states/rational times identify the same continuous paths; continuous statistics then lie in closed W(H_I). No global original basis element is assumed supported; no independence or quotient multiplication is inferred. The new explanation is exactly this subspace argument.

The source mean Jacobian is delta^(a/2), and g_delta=delta^((1-a)/2), giving sqrt(delta) with both constant columns. Strong continuity of S_F and its adjoint follows from the Bessel-unitary Fourier matrix with bounded zero quotient; compact A upgrades conjugation to operator-norm continuity and hence the Bochner integrand. For the unscaled primitive, an increment is bounded by G_B^2 h^(1-1/r) delta^-1/r ||M||Lr(Im); multiplication by sqrt(delta), the sup bound B^(1-1/r), and the theta seminorm B^(1-1/r-theta) give the exact C_B. The strict 1-1/r>theta supplies little-Holder membership and density extends to all H. The observed first-chaos span gives ker L=H_seen^perp and the minimum H preimage norm, without inverting covariance. Finite power mean with p<2<r and the true full/last/empty partition gives delta^(1/p-1/r)n^(1/p-1/r)=(delta n)^(1/p-1/r), n<=2/(delta B), and the exact sqrt(delta) C_B (2/B)^(1/p-1/r) epsilon_J bound. No block independence, radius-uniform tail or stronger source/time limit is inferred.
